title: Faith Plus Anything Nullifies Everything
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: We are saved either by keeping the whole law or by faith in Jesus. There is no door number three.
exhortation: This verse may seem a little out of left field, but when I read it, it really hit me. Circumcision isn't something we talk about much today, but it was normal and even mandatory in Paul's time. It was one simple part of the Jewish faith, and people were asking, "What's the problem with adding it to the Christian faith too? No big deal, right?"

Paul's answer: it's a very big deal. You can have circumcision or you can have Jesus, but you can't have both. He goes on: "I testify again to every man who accepts circumcision that he is obligated to keep the whole law. You are severed from Christ, you who would be justified by the law; you have fallen away from grace... For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but only faith working through love."

Paul is not mincing words. We are saved either by perfectly obeying the law or through faith in Jesus. There's no door number three. It isn't faith plus works or faith plus tradition, because faith plus anything nullifies everything.

Is your faith in the finished work of Jesus? Do you have an answer when your thoughts say, "Maybe I'm not a Christian because of what I've done," or "I can't be a Christian because I'm not good enough. I know I'll fail"? The truth is that we can't save ourselves. Only Jesus can. We may need to repent and turn from sin, but only by turning to Jesus are we truly saved. Because he lived the perfect life, died the perfect death and rose in victory over sin and death, we can be saved by turning to him in faith and putting our trust in him.
prayer: Lord, you have truly paid for everything: all our sin, all our shame, all the wrongs we have done, paid for and washed away at the cross where you shed your precious blood. May we not try to add our works or smuggle in our traditions and the good things we think we can bring. May we lean wholly on your work at the cross, so that you are glorified and we find our joy in you. We look forward to the day when the righteousness poured out for us is fully realized and we see you face to face. Keep that day ever on our minds.

Go with your people today. Fill the hearts of those listening with assurance that you are with them, that you have paid for every sin, and that you look on them with love, joy and satisfaction, not as filthy sinners but as precious children in your sight. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.
